newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algeria's FLN party seek joining government team.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's FLN party seek joining government team.

text.p: Algeria's former sole ruling National Liberation Front (FLN), seen recently as a spent force, is expected to share power in a governing coalition with President Liamine Zeroual's main backers, political sources said on Tuesday.

Politicians bargained over a new government line up after last week's parliamentary election in which the National Democratic Rally (RND), grouping Zeroual supporters, emerged with most seats -- 155 -- in the 380-member National Assembly.
The FLN, which survived in-fighting and bitter criticism over the discredited legacy of its 30-year socialist rule, ranked third with 64 seats.

"The FLN is negotiating the presidency of the National Assembly or the presidency of the cabinet. If the RND insists on keeping both presidencies, the alliance will not be possible," said Al Khabar newspaper, quoting influential FLN leader Abdelkader Hajjar as telling party supporters in Tiaret town.

The party leader Boualem Benhamouda told reporters on Tuesday that a government coalition would be necessary after Algerian political parties "succeed to forge a compromise" over the main issues facing the country.
"For us, the main things remain consultation and coordination between parties before a government coalition would be set up," Benhamouda said.
Amar Tou, another FLN senior leader said the coalition would be discussed after Algeria's 380-member national assembly (lower house) holds its first session on June 15.
"Discussions between President Zeroual and the political parties have not started yet to form a new governemnt," Tou said.
Liberte newspaper said the FLN wanted control of the interior, energy and justice ministries as the price of joining the government.
FLN member Abdelmajid Cherif, a former army general, who is said to be an ally of Zeroual, is tipped as interior minister if the FLN is in the cabinet, the newspaper said.
Tou and Ali Benflis, leading FLN figures, were proposed by the party as energy and justice ministers respectively, the newspaper said.
Incumbent Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia on Tuesday handed his government's resignation to Zeroual, the official APS news agency reported.
It quoted a presidency statement as saying "Zeroual accepted the resignation and asked Ouyahia to handle current affairs."

Zeroual has a free hand to reappoint Ouyahia or replace him, according to the Algerian constitution. Political sources have said it was likely that Ouyahia would be kept in office, at least until after local elections.
Leaders of opposition parties with enough seats to give them bargaining power over government positions kept quiet on Tuesday about their negotiations.
The Islam-oriented Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS) won 69 seats to emerge as the second party, with the Islamist-leaning Nahda party winning 34 seats.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
The outlawed radical Islamic Salvation Front was barred from taking part in last Thursday's election.
